previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis and recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma was admitted for post-procedural monitoring after undergoing CT-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of a left lobe liver tumor. Due to her history of coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia, she received fresh frozen plasma prior to the procedure and was observed in the hospital for three days. The procedure was uncomplicated, but she developed mild post-procedural hepatic encephalopathy, likely triggered by oxycodone, which resolved with increased lactulose and discontinuation of sedating medications. Her hemoglobin dropped from 9.9 to 8.8 g/dL, consistent with post-RFA anemia, and her bilirubin rose to 2.5 mg/dL, reflecting expected liver stress. A transient hyponatremia of 132 mEq/L resolved after holding spironolactone. She had mild atelectasis on chest imaging but no infection, as blood and urine cultures were negative. By discharge, she was alert, ambulatory, and stable, with plans for outpatient follow-up to monitor liver function and blood counts.
